result_text:
I found three superseded ADRs and four header citations of them. All four cite ADR-0023; ADR-0050 and ADR-0125 have none. I opened and read every header myself, either in full or by locating its H1 and first `## ` line; none of this relies on Grep hits alone.

```json
{"superseded": [
  {"id": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"]},
  {"id": "ADR-0050", "successors": ["ADR-0109"]},
  {"id": "ADR-0125", "successors": ["ADR-0144"]}
 ],
 "citations": [
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "ADR-0031", "field": "Related"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "ADR-0032", "field": "Related"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "ADR-0034", "field": "Related"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "RFC-0042", "field": "Related"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "RFC-0050", "field": "Related"}
 ],
 "excluded": [
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "record": "ADR-0042", "why": "successor"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "record": "RFC-0051", "why": "names-successor"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0050", "record": "ADR-0109", "why": "successor"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0125", "record": "ADR-0144", "why": "successor"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0125", "record": "ADR-0061", "why": "names-successor"}
 ],
 "reading_disagreements": [
  "RFC-0050's Related field says itself that 'ADR-0023 is superseded in this session', but it does not name ADR-0042 anywhere in its header (ADR-0042 first appears at line 32). By the Term it is still a header citation. Someone reading for meaning might call it an acknowledged supersession, not a stale citation.",
  "ADR-0061's header names ADR-0125 in its 'Superseded in part' field. That field is not 'Supersedes' or 'Supersedes in part', so the field exclusion does not apply. ADR-0061 is excluded only because the same line also names the successor ADR-0144."
 ]}
```

That is five citations in total: four in `citations` plus RFC-0050. I double-checked RFC-0050 because it is the one most likely to be read differently.

**How I found the superseded ADRs:** I found them by matching a status line of the form `- **Status:** <word>`. All 148 ADR files have exactly one such line. The only other status word besides `Accepted` and `Superseded` is `Rejected` (ADR-0145).

**Hits I left out because they are in the body, not the header:**
- **ADR-0023:** ADR-0035 line 44 and ADR-0043 line 47 (ADR-0043's header also names ADR-0042). RFC-0032 line 249, RFC-0048 from line 251 on (its header ends at line 26).
- **ADR-0050:** ADR-0112 line 38. RFC-0061 line 131. RFC-0102 lines 231–236 (a code block in the body).

No record under `rfc/` mentions ADR-0125. I treated `docs/adr/README.md`, the `*-research.md` files and the files in `rfc/*-notes/` folders as not admitted.

**Ambiguous Terms:**
- The "names none of S's successors" clause covers the whole header, not just the field holding the match. That is what excludes RFC-0051 (ADR-0042 is in the same Related line) and ADR-0061.
- The Term doesn't say what to do with citations inside HTML comments. None came up here.
